headline: Slow oxygen saturation recovery after 6-minute walk test linked to higher risk of death and hospitalisation in COPD
dek: A prospective cohort of 512 COPD patients found that a recovery time of 80 seconds or more was associated with roughly twice the adjusted risk of hospitalisation and mortality.
body:
A prolonged recovery of oxygen saturation (SpO2) after the 6-minute walk test (6MWT) is associated with worse long-term outcomes in people with COPD, according to a study published in Chest.

The researchers, led by Cristóbal Esteban, Nere Larrea-Aguirre and Amaia Aramburu, recruited 512 consecutive patients through the Galdakao University Hospital Respiratory Service. Participants underwent pulmonary function and quadriceps strength assessments, multisensor accelerometry and a 6MWT. Desaturation was defined as a drop in SpO2 of at least 3% from baseline during the test. The recovery time (SpO2-RT) was the time from the end of the test until SpO2 returned to baseline. Of the patients enrolled, 25% were female.

Patients who desaturated during the 6MWT had significantly worse pulmonary function, higher fibrinogen levels, lower quadriceps strength, reduced physical activity and a shorter walking distance. Within this desaturation group, the authors compared patients using an SpO2-RT cut-off of 80 seconds or more. Those with prolonged recovery had more severe pulmonary function impairment, lower physical activity and shorter walking distance.

Over three years of follow-up, longer SpO2-RT was associated with higher mortality (p = .03) and more hospitalisations (p = .0003). In adjusted analyses, prolonged SpO2-RT was associated with an approximately twofold higher risk of both hospitalisation (p = .02) and mortality (p = .04).

The authors concluded that an SpO2-RT of 80 seconds or more identifies a COPD phenotype with diminished respiratory reserve and a higher risk of later exacerbation-related hospitalisation and all-cause mortality. They described SpO2-RT as a simple, accessible metric that enhances the prognostic utility of the standard 6MWT.
key_quote: SpO2-RT is a simple, accessible metric that enhances the prognostic utility of the standard 6MWT.

source.title: Delayed oxygen saturation recovery after the 6-minute walk test: Prognostic implications for COPD patients.
